subproblem.title: Orthogonal projection onto a graph plane via the Gram operator
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, A : R^n -> R^l, J : R^n -> R^(n+l) and T : R^(n+l) -> R^n continuous linear maps such that J v = graphPoint v (A v) for every v in R^n and <T w, v> = <w, J v> for all w in R^(n+l), v in R^n. Then T o J is a unit of the ring L(R^n, R^n) of continuous linear endomorphisms (multiplication = composition), and the orthogonal projection (starProjection) of R^(n+l) onto Gamma_A = span{graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n} equals J o (Ring.inverse(T o J) o T).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (J : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (T : Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Rn n), (∀ v : Rn n, J v = graphPoint v (A v)) → (∀ (w : Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (T w) v = inner ℝ w (J v)) → IsUnit (T ∘L J) ∧ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection = J ∘L Ring.inverse (T ∘L J) ∘L T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 2 (Gamma_A = range J_A), 3 (Gram operator is a unit) and 4 (projection formula), stated for an arbitrary parametrization J of the graph and an arbitrary transpose T of J.

1. J is injective. Suppose J v = J v'. Then graphPoint v (A v) = graphPoint v' (A v'). By definition graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append x y), so for i in Fin n its coordinate at the index Fin.castAdd l i is x_i (Fin.append_left). Comparing these coordinates gives v_i = v'_i for all i, hence v = v'.

2. T o J has trivial kernel. Let v satisfy T(J v) = 0. Applying the hypothesis on T with w = J v gives ||J v||^2 = <J v, J v> = <T(J v), v> = <0, v> = 0, so J v = 0 = J 0 and v = 0 by step 1.

3. T o J is a unit. R^n is finite-dimensional, so a linear endomorphism of R^n with trivial kernel is a unit of the linear endomorphisms (LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot); for continuous linear endomorphisms of the complete space R^n this is equivalent to being a unit of L(R^n, R^n) (ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_toLinearMap). With step 2 this proves IsUnit (T o J), the first conclusion. Put R := Ring.inverse(T o J); since T o J is a unit, (T o J) o R = 1 (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel), i.e. T(J(R u)) = u for every u in R^n.

4. Gamma_A = range J. By the hypothesis on J, the generating set {graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n} equals Set.range J. The range of the linear map J is a submodule whose underlying set is Set.range J (LinearMap.coe_range), and the span of a submodule is itself (Submodule.span_eq). Hence Gamma_A = range J; in particular every z in Gamma_A has the form z = J v.

5. Orthogonality. Fix w in R^(n+l) and put p := J(R(T w)) = (J o (R o T)) w. Then p is in range J = Gamma_A. For z = J v in Gamma_A, using the hypothesis on T twice (with w and with J(R(T w))) and step 3:
 <w - p, J v> = <w, J v> - <J(R(T w)), J v> = <T w, v> - <T(J(R(T w))), v> = <T w, v> - <T w, v> = 0.

6. Conclusion. Gamma_A is a finite-dimensional, hence complete, subspace, so it has an orthogonal projection, and by its characterization (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero: if p is in K and <w - p, z> = 0 for all z in K, then K.starProjection w = p) we get starProjection_(Gamma_A) w = (J o (R o T)) w. Since w is arbitrary, starProjection_(Gamma_A) = J o (Ring.inverse(T o J) o T) (ext), the second conclusion.
proof_key_steps: J is injective (castAdd coordinates of graphPoint v (A v) are v_i)
ker(T o J) = 0 since <T J v, v> = ||J v||^2; finite dimension makes T o J a unit of L(R^n, R^n)
Gamma_A = span(range J) = range J
w - J R T w is orthogonal to every J v because T J R = 1
eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero identifies starProjection with J o Ring.inverse(T o J) o T

audit.reason: Both hypotheses and conclusions match the Lean type. Coordinate injectivity and the transpose identity prove Gram invertibility in the composition ring. Range identification and residual orthogonality then prove the projection formula without assuming the parent or any sibling.

subproblem.title: Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the block operator [[0, H^T],[H, 0]]
subproblem.statement: For natural numbers n, l, a continuous linear H : R^n -> R^l and a continuous linear D : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l) such that D(graphPoint x y) = graphPoint (sum_{i<n} <H e_i, y> e_i) (H x) for all x in R^n, y in R^l (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n): hsNormSq D = 2 hsNormSq H, where hsNormSq B = sum_k ||B E_k||^2 over the standard basis.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (H : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (D : Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), D (graphPoint x y) = graphPoint (∑ i : Fin n, inner ℝ (H (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) y • EuclideanSpace.single i 1) (H x)) → hsNormSq D = 2 * hsNormSq H
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (Hilbert-Schmidt norm), stated for any operator D with the block form [[0, H^T],[H, 0]]. No sibling result is used; proj_fderiv_zero supplies this hypothesis for D = DPi(0)[H] only in the parent assembly.

1. Norms of graph points. ||graphPoint x y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2: on EuclideanSpace, ||z||^2 = sum_k z_k^2 (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq); split the sum over Fin (n+l) into castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add), where the coordinates of graphPoint x y are x_i, resp. y_j (Fin.append_left/right).

2. Standard basis of R^(n+l). Let E_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 in R^(n+l) and f_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1 in R^l. Then E_(castAdd l i) = graphPoint e_i 0 and E_(natAdd n j) = graphPoint 0 f_j. Compare coordinates at the indices castAdd l i' and natAdd n j' (Fin.addCases): E_(castAdd l i) has coordinate 1 exactly at castAdd l i (castAdd is injective, and castAdd l i' is never natAdd n j' because their values satisfy i' < n <= n + j'), which matches the coordinates (e_i)_(i') and 0 of graphPoint e_i 0. Likewise E_(natAdd n j) has coordinate 1 exactly at natAdd n j (natAdd n is injective and never equals castAdd l i'), which matches the coordinates 0 and (f_j)_(j') of graphPoint 0 f_j.

3. Splitting the sum. By definition hsNormSq D = sum_{k in Fin (n+l)} ||D E_k||^2 = sum_{i in Fin n} ||D E_(castAdd l i)||^2 + sum_{j in Fin l} ||D E_(natAdd n j)||^2 (Fin.sum_univ_add).

4. Horizontal columns. For i in Fin n, by step 2 and the hypothesis, D E_(castAdd l i) = D(graphPoint e_i 0) = graphPoint (sum_{i'} <H e_(i'), 0> e_(i')) (H e_i) = graphPoint 0 (H e_i) (<z, 0> = 0). By step 1, ||D E_(castAdd l i)||^2 = ||H e_i||^2.

5. Vertical columns. For j in Fin l, D E_(natAdd n j) = D(graphPoint 0 f_j) = graphPoint (sum_{i'} <H e_(i'), f_j> e_(i')) (H 0) = graphPoint (sum_{i'} (H e_(i'))_j e_(i')) 0, because <z, f_j> = z_j (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right) and H 0 = 0. By step 1, ||D E_(natAdd n j)||^2 = ||sum_{i'} (H e_(i'))_j e_(i')||^2 = sum_{i} (H e_i)_j^2, since the i-th coordinate of sum_{i'} c_(i') e_(i') is c_i (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq).

6. Summation. Combining steps 3-5 and exchanging the finite sums (Finset.sum_comm):
 hsNormSq D = sum_i ||H e_i||^2 + sum_j sum_i (H e_i)_j^2 = sum_i ||H e_i||^2 + sum_i sum_j (H e_i)_j^2 = sum_i ||H e_i||^2 + sum_i ||H e_i||^2 = 2 hsNormSq H,
 using ||z||^2 = sum_j z_j^2 for z in R^l (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq) and hsNormSq H = sum_i ||H e_i||^2 by definition.
proof_key_steps: ||graphPoint x y||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||y||^2
E_(castAdd l i) = graphPoint e_i 0 and E_(natAdd n j) = graphPoint 0 f_j
Split hsNormSq D over castAdd/natAdd indices (Fin.sum_univ_add)
Horizontal columns contribute ||H e_i||^2; vertical columns contribute sum_i (H e_i)_j^2
Exchange the finite sums: hsNormSq D = hsNormSq H + hsNormSq H

audit.reason: The operator hypothesis and norm conclusion match exactly. The proof derives both standard-basis block contributions and exchanges finite sums to obtain the factor 2. It is independent of the derivative theorem, whose conclusion supplies its hypothesis precisely in the parent assembly.

subproblem.title: Hand-built continuous linear transpose between Euclidean spaces
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers n, m there is a continuous linear map tau : L(R^n, R^m) -> L(R^m, R^n) (both spaces of continuous linear maps with the operator norm) such that for every continuous linear L : R^n -> R^m and all w in R^m, v in R^n: <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v>. Here R^k = EuclideanSpace R (Fin k) = Rn k with its standard inner product.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n m : ℕ), ∃ τ : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn m) →L[ℝ] (Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn n), ∀ (L : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn m) (w : Rn m) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (τ L w) v = inner ℝ w (L v)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (Transpose), with the construction made explicit. ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch05.Submission, so the transpose is built from the standard basis.

1. Notation. For i in Fin n let e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n. These are the vectors of the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) R, so every v in R^n satisfies v = sum_i v_i e_i (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr), and <e_i, u> = u_i for every u in R^n (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left).

2. Definition of tau_0. For L in L(R^n, R^m) put tau_0(L) := sum_{i in Fin n} (innerSL R (L e_i)).smulRight e_i in L(R^m, R^n). Thus tau_0(L) w = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i. Each summand is a continuous linear functional w |-> <L e_i, w> times the fixed vector e_i, so tau_0(L) is a continuous linear map R^m -> R^n.

3. tau_0 is R-linear in L. For L, L' and every w: tau_0(L + L') w = sum_i <L e_i + L' e_i, w> e_i = sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i + sum_i <L' e_i, w> e_i = tau_0(L) w + tau_0(L') w (additivity of the inner product in its first argument, add_smul, Finset.sum_add_distrib). For c in R: tau_0(c L) w = sum_i <c L e_i, w> e_i = sum_i (c <L e_i, w>) e_i = c tau_0(L) w (real_inner_smul_left, smul_smul, Finset.smul_sum). Hence tau_0 is a linear map L(R^n, R^m) -> L(R^m, R^n) (ext on w reduces both identities to the computations above).

4. Continuity. The space L(R^n, R^m) is finite-dimensional, so every linear map out of it into a normed space is continuous; LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap turns tau_0 into a continuous linear map tau with tau(L) = tau_0(L) for all L.

5. Adjoint identity. Fix L, w, v. By step 2, <tau(L) w, v> = <sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> <e_i, v> = sum_i <L e_i, w> v_i. On the other hand, by step 1 and linearity of L, L v = sum_i v_i L e_i, so <w, L v> = sum_i v_i <w, L e_i> = sum_i v_i <L e_i, w> (symmetry of the real inner product, real_inner_comm). The two sums agree term by term (commutativity of multiplication), so <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v>.

6. Hence tau is the required continuous linear map, which proves the existence statement.
proof_key_steps: Define tau(L) w := sum_i <L e_i, w> e_i via innerSL/smulRight with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1
tau is linear in L (additivity and homogeneity of the inner product in its first slot)
tau is continuous because L(R^n, R^m) is finite-dimensional (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap)
Adjoint identity <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v> by expanding v = sum_i v_i e_i

audit.reason: The exact type matches the fully quantified prose. The finite basis construction proves real linearity, finite-dimensional continuity, and the stated transpose identity. It uses neither siblings nor the parent and covers zero dimensions.

subproblem.title: The graph-plane projection map is C^2
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers n, l, the map Pi : L(R^n, R^l) -> L(R^(n+l), R^(n+l)), A |-> starProjection of Gamma_A = span{graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n}, is C^2 (ContDiff R 2), both spaces carrying the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), ContDiff ℝ 2 (fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 0 (graphPoint), 2 (parametrization), 3-4 (Gram operator, projection formula; here supplied by the sibling gram_projection) and 5 (smoothness).

1. Splitting graphPoint. Let Phi := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd)^(-1) : R^n x R^l -> R^(n+l), a continuous linear equivalence. Then graphPoint x y = Phi(x, y): compare coordinates; every index of Fin (n+l) is Fin.castAdd l j or Fin.natAdd n k (Fin.addCases), and at these indices both sides equal x_j, resp. y_k (Fin.append_left/right and the definition of finAddEquivProd). Put iota := Phi o inl in L(R^n, R^(n+l)) and kappa := Phi o inr in L(R^l, R^(n+l)). Since (x, y) = (x, 0) + (0, y) and Phi is additive, graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y for all x, y.

2. Transpose. By the sibling transpose_clm with m = n + l (Amb n l and Rn (n+l) are the same type EuclideanSpace R (Fin (n+l))), there is a continuous linear tau : L(R^n, R^(n+l)) -> L(R^(n+l), R^n) with <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v> for all L, w, v.

3. Parametrization. For A in L(R^n, R^l) put J_A := iota + kappa o A in L(R^n, R^(n+l)). By step 1, J_A v = iota v + kappa(A v) = graphPoint v (A v) for every v.

4. Projection formula. Apply the sibling gram_projection to (n, l, A, J_A, tau(J_A)); its two hypotheses are step 3 and step 2 with L = J_A. Hence, for every A, G_A := tau(J_A) o J_A is a unit of L(R^n, R^n) and Pi(A) = J_A o (Ring.inverse(G_A) o tau(J_A)). Therefore Pi = F as functions on L(R^n, R^l), where F(A) := J_A o (Ring.inverse(G_A) o tau(J_A)); it suffices to show that F is C^2.

5. Smooth building blocks. A |-> J_A is the constant iota plus the continuous linear map A |-> kappa o A (ContinuousLinearMap.compL R R^n R^l R^(n+l) kappa), hence C^2 (contDiff_const.add, ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff). A |-> tau(J_A) is the continuous linear map tau composed with a C^2 map, hence C^2 (ContDiff.comp). A |-> G_A = tau(J_A) o J_A is C^2 because composition of two C^2 operator-valued maps is C^2 (ContDiff.clm_comp).

6. Smooth inversion. L(R^n, R^n) is a complete normed R-algebra (finite dimension), so the instance HasSummableGeomSeries holds and Ring.inverse is C^2 at every unit (contDiffAt_ringInverse). Fix A. By step 4, G_A = (u : L(R^n, R^n)) for some unit u, so Ring.inverse is C^2 at G_A, and by the chain rule (ContDiffAt.comp) with the C^2 map A |-> G_A of step 5, A |-> Ring.inverse(G_A) is C^2 at A. Since A was arbitrary, A |-> Ring.inverse(G_A) is C^2 (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).

7. Conclusion. Two applications of ContDiff.clm_comp, first to A |-> Ring.inverse(G_A) and A |-> tau(J_A) and then to A |-> J_A and the result, show that F is C^2. Since Pi = F (step 4), Pi is C^2.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y with iota = Phi o inl, kappa = Phi o inr, Phi = finAddEquivProd^-1
J_A := iota + kappa o A parametrizes Gamma_A; tau from transpose_clm
gram_projection gives Pi(A) = J_A o Ring.inverse(G_A) o tau(J_A) with G_A a unit, so Pi = F
A |-> J_A, tau(J_A), G_A are C^2 (affine map, CLM, ContDiff.clm_comp)
Ring.inverse is C^2 at units (contDiffAt_ringInverse), so A |-> Ring.inverse(G_A) and then F are C^2

audit.reason: This is exactly the parent's first conjunct. Both declared dependencies are applied with their required hypotheses. Affine parametrization, continuous linear transpose, operator composition, and smooth inversion at every Gram unit establish global C² regularity without a gap.

subproblem.title: Derivative of the graph-plane projection at A = 0
subproblem.statement: For natural numbers n, l, H in L(R^n, R^l), x in R^n and y in R^l, with Pi(A) = starProjection of span{graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n} and DPi(0) = fderiv R Pi 0: DPi(0)[H](graphPoint x y) = graphPoint (sum_{i<n} <H e_i, y> e_i) (H x), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 in R^n. (In block form with respect to R^n x R^l, DPi(0)[H] = [[0, H^T],[H, 0]].)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (H : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (x : Rn n) (y : Rn ℓ), fderiv ℝ (fun A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection) 0 H (graphPoint x y) = graphPoint (∑ i : Fin n, inner ℝ (H (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) y • EuclideanSpace.single i 1) (H x)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 0, 2, 4 (here via the sibling gram_projection), 6 (values at A = 0) and 7 (derivative at 0), followed by evaluation at graphPoint x y.

1. Splitting graphPoint. Phi := (EuclideanSpace.finAddEquivProd)^(-1) : R^n x R^l -> R^(n+l), a continuous linear equivalence, satisfies graphPoint x y = Phi(x, y): compare coordinates; every index of Fin (n+l) is Fin.castAdd l j or Fin.natAdd n k (Fin.addCases), and at these indices both sides equal x_j, resp. y_k (Fin.append_left/right and the definition of finAddEquivProd). Put iota := Phi o inl and kappa := Phi o inr (continuous linear). Since (x, y) = (x, 0) + (0, y) and Phi is additive, graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y; in particular iota v = graphPoint v 0 and kappa z = graphPoint 0 z.

2. Inner products of graph points. <graphPoint x y, graphPoint x' y'> = <x, x'> + <y, y'>. Indeed the inner product of EuclideanSpace is the coordinate sum sum_k a_k b_k (PiLp.inner_apply); split the sum over Fin (n+l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add), where the coordinates are x_i, x'_i, resp. y_j, y'_j (Fin.append_left/right).

3. Transpose and pi. By the sibling transpose_clm with m = n + l there is a continuous linear tau with <tau(L) w, v> = <w, L v>. Put pi := tau(iota). Using nondegeneracy of the inner product (ext_inner_right: if <a, u> = <b, u> for all u then a = b):
 (a) pi(iota v) = v, since for all u: <pi(iota v), u> = <iota v, iota u> = <graphPoint v 0, graphPoint u 0> = <v, u> + <0, 0> = <v, u>;
 (b) pi(kappa z) = 0, since for all u: <pi(kappa z), u> = <kappa z, iota u> = <graphPoint 0 z, graphPoint u 0> = <0, u> + <z, 0> = 0 = <0, u>.

4. Reduction to an explicit formula. For A in L(R^n, R^l) put J_A := iota + kappa o A, so J_A v = graphPoint v (A v) (step 1) and J_0 = iota. Apply the sibling gram_projection to (n, l, A, J_A, tau(J_A)) (hypotheses: J_A v = graphPoint v (A v), and the identity of step 3 with L = J_A): for every A, Pi(A) = F(A) := J_A o (R_A o tau(J_A)), where G_A := tau(J_A) o J_A and R_A := Ring.inverse(G_A). Hence Pi = F as functions and fderiv R Pi 0 = fderiv R F 0.

5. Derivatives at 0. Let K := ContinuousLinearMap.compL R R^n R^l R^(n+l) kappa, i.e. K(H) = kappa o H.
 (a) A |-> J_A = iota + K(A) has derivative K at 0 (constant plus continuous linear map; HasFDerivAt.const_add of K.hasFDerivAt).
 (b) A |-> tau(J_A) has derivative tau o K at 0 (chain rule; tau is continuous linear).
 (c) By the product rule for compositions of operator-valued maps (HasFDerivAt.clm_comp: the derivative of A |-> c(A) o d(A) is H |-> c(0) o d'(H) + c'(H) o d(0)), A |-> G_A has at 0 the derivative H |-> tau(J_0) o (kappa o H) + tau(kappa o H) o J_0. This is the zero map: for all H and v, tau(J_0)(kappa(H v)) = pi(kappa(H v)) = 0 by 3(b), and tau(kappa o H)(iota v) = 0 because for all u, <tau(kappa o H)(iota v), u> = <iota v, kappa(H u)> = <graphPoint v 0, graphPoint 0 (H u)> = <v, 0> + <0, H u> = 0 (step 2). So A |-> G_A has derivative 0 at 0.
 (d) G_0 = tau(iota) o iota = pi o iota = 1 by 3(a); hence R_0 = Ring.inverse 1 = 1 (Ring.inverse_one).
 (e) Ring.inverse has a derivative D at the unit 1 = G_0 (hasFDerivAt_ringInverse applied to the unit 1, whose value is 1 = G_0). By the chain rule A |-> R_A = Ring.inverse(G_A) has derivative D o 0 = 0 at 0.
 (f) Applying the product rule twice to F(A) = J_A o (R_A o tau(J_A)), F has at 0 the derivative
 H |-> J_0 o (R_0 o tau(kappa o H) + 0 o tau(J_0)) + (kappa o H) o (R_0 o tau(J_0)) = iota o tau(kappa o H) + kappa o H o pi,
 using J_0 = iota, R_0 = 1 and tau(J_0) = pi. Therefore (HasFDerivAt.fderiv and step 4) fderiv R Pi 0 H = iota o tau(kappa o H) + kappa o H o pi.

6. Evaluation at w := graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y.
 (a) pi w = pi(iota x) + pi(kappa y) = x + 0 = x by step 3.
 (b) tau(kappa o H) w = sum_i <H e_i, y> e_i. For every u in R^n: <tau(kappa o H) w, u> = <w, kappa(H u)> = <graphPoint x y, graphPoint 0 (H u)> = <x, 0> + <y, H u> = <y, H u> (step 2). Expanding u = sum_i u_i e_i (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr for EuclideanSpace.basisFun), <y, H u> = sum_i u_i <y, H e_i> = sum_i <H e_i, y> <e_i, u> = <sum_i <H e_i, y> e_i, u>, using <e_i, u> = u_i (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left) and symmetry of the real inner product. By nondegeneracy the two vectors coincide.
 (c) Hence fderiv R Pi 0 H (graphPoint x y) = iota(tau(kappa o H) w) + kappa(H(pi w)) = iota(sum_i <H e_i, y> e_i) + kappa(H x) = graphPoint (sum_i <H e_i, y> e_i) (H x) by step 1.
proof_key_steps: graphPoint x y = iota x + kappa y and <graphPoint x y, graphPoint x' y'> = <x, x'> + <y, y'>
pi := tau(iota) satisfies pi o iota = 1 and pi o kappa = 0
gram_projection: Pi(A) = J_A o Ring.inverse(G_A) o tau(J_A) with J_A = iota + kappa o A, so fderiv Pi 0 = fderiv F 0
DG(0) = 0 by orthogonality of iota and kappa; G_0 = 1, R_0 = 1 and DR(0) = 0 via hasFDerivAt_ringInverse
Product rule: DPi(0)[H] = iota o tau(kappa o H) + kappa o H o pi
On graphPoint x y: pi w = x and tau(kappa o H) w = sum_i <H e_i, y> e_i, giving graphPoint (H^T y) (H x)

audit.reason: The quantified evaluation formula exactly matches the prose. Orthogonality proves DG(0)=0, inversion gives DR(0)=0, and the product rule yields the block derivative. Basis expansion identifies its transpose block using only the declared siblings; no reliance on proj_contdiff or the parent is hidden.
